34 A student assembles the circuit shown.
lamp 1
lamp 2
Which row describes the state of the two lamps?
lamp 1
lamp 2
A
off
off
B
on
off
C
off
on
D
on
on

hints: Notice the direction of the single diode in series with lamp 1 and the two opposite-facing diodes in series with lamp 2.
Recall a diode conducts only when conventional current enters in the direction its triangle points, and blocks reverse current.
Check which diode in each parallel branch is forward-biased for current flowing down from the top rail to the bottom rail.
walkthrough: Identify the three parallel branches across the cell: the cell on the left, lamp 1 with one diode in the middle, and lamp 2 with two parallel diodes on the right.
State the diode rule: forward bias with current in the direction of the triangle gives conduction, reverse bias gives almost no current.
For the middle branch, the diode triangle points downward, the same sense as current flowing from the top rail through lamp 1 to the bottom rail, so this branch conducts and lamp 1 lights.
For the right branch, the two diodes are in parallel but point in opposite directions, so one points downward and one points upward.
The downward-pointing diode of that pair is forward-biased for downward current, providing a conducting path in series with lamp 2, so lamp 2 also lights despite the other diode being reverse-biased.
Both lamps therefore have current and light. This is option D.

A.explanation: Both lamps are not off because the right-hand branch always has a forward-biased diode and the middle diode is also forward-biased.

B.explanation: Lamp 2 is not off because one of the two opposite diodes in parallel is forward-biased for either battery polarity.

C.explanation: Lamp 1 is not off because its single series diode is oriented to allow conventional current from the top rail to the bottom rail.

D.explanation: Both branches have a forward-biased diode path so conventional current flows through lamp 1 and through lamp 2, lighting both.
